title: Pro-etale closed-support triangle before constructible restriction
statement:
Let $T$ be Noetherian, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a
closed immersion, and
let $j$ be its open complement. For a finite ring $A$, let
$Ri^!$ denote the right adjoint of the
direct image $i_*$ on the
pro-etale sites, taken on
the ambient ordinary derived categories, and let $Rj_*$ and $j^*$
be the direct image and the
inverse image of the open immersion $j$. In addition to the
open–closed triangle,
one has

$$
i_*Ri^!K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K
\longrightarrow i_*Ri^!K[1]
\qquad(K\in D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)).
$$

No constructibility of $Ri^!K$ is part of this assertion.

proof.text: Use finiteCoefficientRealization_isEquivalence_ring in the recorded finite-module module, which applies to arbitrary finite rings. Construct its explicit inverse by restriction along finiteCoefficientScalarMap. The module-sheafification Hom equivalence gives its adjunction. Under this inverse, finiteModulePushforward is naturally the existing fixed-scalar lowerStar: the direct-image ring map preserves constant scalars by the sheafification adjunction, and the component comparison is the identity on sections. Conjugate the two adjunctions to obtain the corresponding pullback comparison. All four comparison functors and their naturality and linearity proofs are constructed in Lean; no comparison theorem is assumed.

proof.text: Noetherianity of T and the open embedding give a Noetherian underlying space of U, so j is quasi-compact by Mathlib. Transfer exactness and full faithfulness of the closed direct image from the fixed-scalar source API through the explicit equivalence of step 1. In that same source API, isZero_upperStar_lowerStar_of_disjoint gives open restriction of closed direct image zero, and isZero_of_isZero_upperStar_of_isCompl gives joint detection of zero. Transfer both through the constructed comparisons and reflect zero objects along the fully faithful restriction functor. Open direct image is fully faithful because its ordinary counit is invertible.

proof.text: The recorded Grothendieck module-sheaf theorem supplies K-injective resolutions in the required universe. Use the source library exact-left-adjoint derived-adjunction API on the actual finiteModuleAdjunction for j. Direct images preserve K-injectives as right adjoints of exact pullbacks. Their full faithfulness therefore descends to the unbounded right-derived functors; exact closed direct image is identified with its termwise mapDerivedCategory. Hence the derived open counit is invertible. This uses the existing implementations in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.RightDerivedFunctor.Adjunction and FullyFaithful, rather than constructing new derived functors.

proof.text: On homology, exact pullbacks and pushforwards commute with cohomology. Thus the vanishing and joint-zero detection in step 2 hold in the derived categories. If J(K)=0, complete the closed inverse-image adjunction unit K to i_*i^*K to a distinguished triangle. Closed inverse image inverts this unit by full faithfulness of closed direct image; open inverse image inverts it because both its endpoints are zero. The cone is zero by joint detection, so the unit is invertible and K lies in the essential image of i_*. This is a complete private Lean argument, not a new assumed essential-image statement.

proof.text: Apply the proved source-library Recollement.isLeftAdjoint theorem to the fully faithful termwise closed pushforward, the derived open adjunction with invertible counit, and the vanishing and essential-image facts of step 4. It supplies a right adjoint of i_*. Apply Recollement.exists_distTriang_counit_unit to this adjunction: its proof completes the open unit to a triangle, identifies its fibre in the closed essential image and uses Hom orthogonality to identify the first map with the closed counit. Finally Functor.mapDerivedCategoryFactors supplies both requested natural localization isomorphisms. The unit record has no realized statement or proof-step nodes, so this replaces only the below-unit auxiliary proof route.
